Deutsche 話 Microsoft F2Q 嘅 Azure 增長有幾多？同 guidance 比點？

text: Deutsche预计微软F2Q Azure营收同比增长约26%，至220亿美元左右，高于市场普遍预期的25%。该增速虽略低于上一季度的29%，但仍高于管理层给出的22%-24%的指引中值，反映出云业务的强劲韧性。

What We Liked / What We're watching on the Quarter
Revenue/Bookings
(+) F2Q revenue of $81.3bn was 1.5% above the midpoint of guidance, with upside 
concentrated in PBP & IC segments. On a constant currency basis, growth ticked 
down ~1.5pts sequentially to +15% y/y.
(+) Commercial Bookings rose +228% y/y @cc. This was primarily driven by the 
previously disclosed larger Azure commit from OpenAI, alongside benefit from the 
recent Anthropic commitment and "healthy growth" across core annuity sales 
motions on a lower expiry base when adjusted for OpenAI contracts in the prior 
year. Commercial RPO ended the quarter +110% y/y to $625bn; ~45% of the total 
balance is now attributed to commits from OpenAI, with the remaining core 55% 
growing +28% y/y. Total Commercial cRPO now stands at +39% y/y, up from +21% 
a year prior.
Business Lines
(=) Azure growth of +38% y/y @CC was 1pt above guidance (37%), but likely a touch 
shy of buyside expectations that we believe were closer to ~+39%. Upside to 
guidance was a result of efficiency gains across the fleet enabling reallocation of 
some capacity from other segments to monetizable Azure demand. We underscore 
that these results were once again limited by supply constraints as mgmt. noted the 
need to balance increasing Azure demand with growing needs across 1P services, 
increasing allocation to R&D teams, and replacement of end-of-life equipment.
(=) M365 Commercial Cloud growth of +14% y/y came in line with the high end of 
guidance +13-14% y/y @cc, with growth once again driven by a combination of 
seat growth (+6% y/y) and ARPU expansion. ARPU expansion also continues to be 
attributed to E5 momentum and then M365 Copilot. This quarter was also the first 
time mgmt. disclosed M365 copilot paid seats, which sit at 15m as of F2Q.
(+) Server Products grew +1% y/y @CC, much better compared to guidance for a 
LSD-MSD decline driven by demand for Micros

Microsoft reported another solid result for F2Q, but it ultimately fell short of more 
lofty market expectations, in particular for Azure growth. While most investors 
continue to hone in on this as the most important KPI, mgmt. again made it clear 
Azure is bearing the brunt of current supply constraints as they prioritize GPU 
allocation in support of AI usage in first-party apps and R&D to accelerate product 
innovation in pursuit of higher margin, recurring software opportunities up the 
stack. So while Azure growth still came in 1pt above guidance at +38% y/y @CC, 
this was shy of what we believe was a buyside bogey of >39%+ and what mgmt. 
indicated would have been >40% had they allocated all incremental GPU capacity 
in F1H26 to Azure. Importantly, we'd highlight Azure is still growing well above the 
market, guided to sustain 37-38% growth in F3Q and we believe can likely persist 
near here for several more quarters off a higher base.
From a margin and LTV perspective we believe the application layer has and is still 
generally perceived as highly strategic ground on which Microsoft has incumbent 
advantages. But we'd argue it is also the last area to see tangible benefits as AI 
monetization works its way up the stack, and is more than ever viewed as at risk of 
disruption and/or devaluation, which is weighing on sentiment. That story has yet 
to play out in our view, so while foregoing Azure revenue now for high-margin 
application and consumer SW opportunity ahead seems a sensible long-term 
strategy, it puts the onus on Microsoft to deliver before it will get credit. We continue 
to see more evidence of steadily growing traction, including new disclosure this 
quarter of 15m paid M365 Copilot seats (accelerating q/q and +160% y/y), paid 
GitHub Copilot subs now up to 4.7m (+75% y/y) and >100k medical providers using
